resale_co.notes: No Borough resale Certificate of Occupancy or resale inspection for 1-2 family homes was found. The Borough forms page (updated July 2026) lists only the 'Smoke and Fire Certificates of Occupancy', which the Borough now sends to NJ DCA, plus rental registration, zoning permits and a zoning verification letter request. The Code Enforcement page covers property maintenance and vacant property registration only. The 2026 ordinance index (Ord. 01-2026 to 08-2026) has nothing on resale inspections. The Borough code is on Municode, which blocked every fetch this time; an earlier check reported a rental certificate of occupancy (section 15.04.065, rental units only) and no resale inspection, but that could not be re-read now. Silence is not proof, so status stays not_found. The annual rental registration and rental certificate are rental programs, not resale requirements.

requirements: Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms as required by N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 for 1 and 2 family homes (the Borough and DCA pages found do not list the details)

authorities.name: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many business days before the change of occupant the request is received: more than 10 business days for the lowest fee.

fire_cert.notes: The Borough's own notice sends all smoke/fire certificates to NJ DCA, and the DCA state-towns list (revised 7/17/2026) and the July 2026 LEA registry (code S) agree that the State is the enforcing agency. Fees are the state fees in N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) as published in the NJ Register (50 N.J.R. 729(a)); the DCA portal shows the charge at checkout. The DCA fire directory lists (609) 633-6132 for the state fire official; the Bureau page lists (609) 633-6106. An older local Bureau of Fire Safety fee schedule in the Borough code appears superseded by the move to DCA and is not listed. The 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped the portable fire extinguisher from the sale certificate.
